# phasetwo_cluster_ip_rules (Resource)

IP allow and deny rules for a dedicated cluster.

This is a singleton holding all three rule lists, because the API replaces a whole category at a time and has no per-rule delete. Declare at most one of these per cluster — a second would silently fight the first.

Every category is sent on each apply, so removing a block from configuration removes those rules. An empty category means no rules in it.

~> An empty `admin_allow` means the admin console is reachable from anywhere. Adding the first entry restricts it to exactly that list — make sure it covers you before applying, or you will lock yourself out of the console.

The number of rules a cluster may hold depends on its tier: none on `starter`, 2 on `premium`, unlimited on `enterprise`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# One of these per cluster: it holds every rule list, because the API replaces a whole category
# at a time.
resource "phasetwo_cluster_ip_rules" "main" {
  cluster_id = phasetwo_cluster.main.id

  # Careful: once this is non-empty the admin console is reachable only from these addresses.
  admin_allow {
    alias   = "office"
    address = "203.0.113.0/24"
  }

  admin_allow {
    alias   = "vpn"
    address = "198.51.100.7"
  }

  realm_block {
    alias   = "known-abuse"
    address = "192.0.2.0/24"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) ID of the cluster.

### Optional

- `admin_allow` (Block List) Addresses allowed to reach the cluster's admin console. When empty, the console is not IP-restricted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--admin_allow))
- `realm_allow` (Block List) Addresses allowed to reach the cluster's realm endpoints. When empty, the realm endpoints are not IP-restricted. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--realm_allow))
- `realm_block` (Block List) Addresses blocked from reaching the cluster's realm endpoints. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--realm_block))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `cluster_id` — the rules are a property of the cluster rather than a resource with its own identity.

<a id="nestedblock--admin_allow"></a>
### Nested Schema for `admin_allow`

Required:

- `address` (String) IP address or CIDR block, e.g. `203.0.113.4` or `203.0.113.0/24`.
- `alias` (String) Human-readable label for the rule.


<a id="nestedblock--realm_allow"></a>
### Nested Schema for `realm_allow`

Required:

- `address` (String) IP address or CIDR block, e.g. `203.0.113.4` or `203.0.113.0/24`.
- `alias` (String) Human-readable label for the rule.


<a id="nestedblock--realm_block"></a>
### Nested Schema for `realm_block`

Required:

- `address` (String) IP address or CIDR block, e.g. `203.0.113.4` or `203.0.113.0/24`.
- `alias` (String) Human-readable label for the rule.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import phasetwo_cluster_ip_rules.main 4f8c1e2a-0000-0000-0000-000000000000
```
